8.0.s.en: 1. Their discipline by the attack of enemies upon them:

8.0.0.en: 1 "Set the trumpet to thy mouth. He shall come as an eagle against the house of the LORD, because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law.

8.0.1.en: "Set the trumpet to thy mouth. He shall come as an eagle against the house of the LORD" [1].

8.0.2.en: When God opened the eyes of the prophet's insight, he perceived the bitterness that would befall the people because they refused the remedy from the hand of their true Physician. His soul groaned within him, and he did not know what to do, but God commanded him to take the trumpet and put it to his mouth, for the time of warning had come. He asked him to sound the trumpet so that all the people might gather and see the enemy attacking like a swift eagle that swoops down upon its prey and soars in the air.

8.0.3.en: Lest the people think that God would not allow them to be taken captive, since they are a people chosen by God, God Himself affirmed, "as an eagle against the house of the LORD." It is as though He were saying: I know that you are the house of God (Heb 3:6), but I have allowed the enemy to swoop down upon you like an eagle because you have corrupted My sanctuary and defiled it. I love My house and dwell in it and keep it by My angels, but I send the enemy upon it like an eagle that swoops down to seize and soar, if you dare against Me and despise My sanctuaries.

8.1.0.en: 1 "Set the trumpet to thy mouth. He shall come as an eagle against the house of the LORD, because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law. 2 Israel shall cry unto me, My God, we know thee. 3 Israel hath cast off the thing that is good: the enemy shall pursue him. 4 They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not: of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off. 5 Thy calf, O Samaria, hath cast thee off; mine anger is kindled against them: how long will it be ere they attain to innocency? 6 For from Israel was it also: the workman made it; therefore it is not God: but the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.

8.1.1.en: What befalls them, although by God's permission, is something that they themselves bring upon themselves, destroying themselves with their own hands. This is what the Lord declares to them, explaining the reasons for their discipline:

8.1.2.en: First: He says, "because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my law" [1]. It is as though He were saying: I chose you as a bride for Myself and made with you the covenant of marriage, but you betrayed the covenant and broke it. I chose you as sons and gave you My law as a fatherly commandment, but you disobeyed My commandment and despised My fatherhood.

8.1.3.en: Second: At the very time when they betrayed the covenant and disobeyed the commandment, they deceived themselves with an outward show of worship without spirit, for He says: "Israel shall cry unto me, My God, we know thee" [2]. They reject Him by their deeds and their hearts, and seek Him with their lips. They turn their backs to Him in their daily life, but when they gather for worship they cry out to Him, saying, "My God, we know thee," as though they wanted to remind Him that they are the chosen people whom God will not allow to be harmed!

8.2.0.en: Third: Their betrayal of the marriage covenant, or their disobedience to the fatherly commandment, is not done out of weakness as an incidental matter, but springs from a defiled heart, an evil will, and an inward hatred of the holy life, for He says: "Israel hath cast off the thing that is good: the enemy shall pursue him" [3]. Because Israel hated the holy life, God therefore delivered His house, that is, His people, who ought to have been holy to the Lord, to the king of Assyria, who carried the northern kingdom into captivity; and when Judah hated the Lord, God delivered the kingdom of Judah, with the city of Jerusalem and its temple that it contained, into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar. In any case, if God has known us as His own people, then when we refuse in practice to know Him, He delivers us to discipline, saying to us: "You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities" (Amos 3:2).

8.3.0.en: Fourth: He adds to their hatred of the good the following error: "They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not" [4]. In our study of the previous chapter we saw that the king signifies the human will that reigns over the whole man and controls him, and that the princes signify man's energies and gifts, especially those of leadership. Their setting up of kings from themselves and not from God signifies their living according to their own will, and their ordering the affairs of their lives without resorting to God or seeking His counsel. As for His saying, "they have made princes, and I knew it not," it means that their gifts and energies work not for the sake of the Kingdom of God, so they became strangers to Him, neither knowing God nor deserving that God should know them.

8.3.1.en: God in His love for us wants us to return to Him in everything, so that we do not set up within us kings or princes without His counsel, but rather do as Jephthah, who "uttered all his words before the LORD in Mizpeh" (Judg 11:11), so that it may not be said of us, "neither look unto the Holy One of Israel" (Isa 31:1). As St. John Chrysostom says: [He longs greatly for us always to take refuge in Him, and to ask everything from Him, and without Him to do nothing and utter no word... For this is the habit of lovers, who ask their beloved to be bound to them, so that they do nothing and utter no word without them.]

8.3.2.en: What we say concerning the kings and princes within the soul, that is, the human will, energies and gifts, we repeat concerning the Church as the congregation of believers, for it is not fitting to appoint a bishop or a priest without the counsel of the Lord. St. Cyprian wrote in one of his letters about the heretics: [There are undoubtedly bishops who were appointed not according to the will of God, but are like those outside the Church. These were appointed contrary to the order of the Gospel and its tradition, as the Lord said through the prophets: "Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that they take counsel, but not of me; and make a covenant, but not by my Spirit, that they may add sin to sin" [(Isa 30:1) the Septuagint]]. And he wrote in another letter: [Sometimes unworthy bishops are ordained; these are ordained not according to the will of God but according to human arrangement, so that the ordination takes place in an unlawful and ungodly manner, which grieves God, as was declared in the prophet Hosea.]

8.3.3.en: The Lord continues His rebuke of His people, saying: "of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off" [4]. They made images of the pagan gods, and so lost the silver and gold they possessed in order to acquire God's wrath and their own destruction, as though they were buying with their silver and gold what would cut them off and destroy them.

8.3.4.en: If silver signifies the word of God purified seven times, and gold signifies the spiritual life, then some often misuse the word of God and the spiritual life so that they become for their destruction instead of their spiritual edification, as when they set up the word of preaching, or practice the ascetic life, not in a spirit of humility before God but in a spirit of self-importance for the sake of their own honor.

8.4.0.en: He also says: "Thy calf, O Samaria, hath cast thee off" [5]. This refers to the beginning of the revolt against the kingdom of David, when Jeroboam split off from the kingdom, and, fearing that the people would turn their hearts back to Jerusalem and kill him and follow Rehoboam king of Judah, he made two calves of gold (1 Kgs 12:28), setting up one in Bethel and the other in Dan, and said to the people: "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt" (1 Kgs 12:28). It seems that the setting up of the calves was not at first intended for the worship of idols, but they thought that Jehovah dwelt upon them; gradually, however, it turned into idol worship. It seems that the calf at Dan was moved to Samaria when it became the capital of the northern kingdom. In any case, although God permitted Jeroboam to carry out his counsel against Rehoboam the son of Solomon as a discipline for the sins of Solomon, Jeroboam is condemned for doing this, especially for setting up sanctuaries outside Jerusalem which became dangerous centers for spreading idol worship and its abominations.

8.5.0.en: The calf of Samaria has gone rancid, or been cast off, having lost its splendor even in the eyes of its worshippers, because it could not save itself nor deliver them from the hand of the king of Assyria. "The calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces" [6], that is, it will be shattered like an earthen vessel into fragments that cannot be mended. They set up for themselves a god that is the work of their own hands, and it was shattered and shattered them with it. It is a bitter picture of many who make for themselves out of their gold a calf in their Samaria, that is, they set up themselves as gods in their corrupt hearts. This self, having become a god, has taken the place of the living God in the inner Jerusalem, and therefore it falls and is shattered from the height of its arrogance.

8.5.1.en: God's anger was kindled against them [5], because they took His gold, which He had given them to be their gold, and instead of using it for the glory of God they made with it a calf in their Samaria, without beauty, which is shattered into fragments without remedy... They reject the holy God and cannot endure purity... "How long will it be ere they attain to innocency?" [5].

8.6.s.en: 3. Their loss of satisfaction and joy

8.6.0.en: 7 "For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: it hath no stalk: the bud shall yield no meal: if so be it yield, the strangers shall swallow it up. 8 Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure. 9 For they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath hired lovers. 10 Though they have hired among the nations, now will I gather them, and they shall be released a little from the burden of the king of princes.

8.6.1.en: After announcing their discipline by an enemy who attacks their land and plunders them of everything, and revealing to them the reasons for the discipline, He concluded His speech by declaring that evil does not satisfy man nor give him joy, saying: "They have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind" [7]. They endured hardships in preparing everything for sowing, and behold, they sow wind; and when they wished to reap, they gathered turmoil, anxieties and gloom (the whirlwind). Truly "they labour in vain" (Isa 65:23), "labour for the wind" (Eccl 5:16), "and weary themselves for very vanity" (Hab 2:13). As the Apostle says, those who sow to the flesh reap corruption (Gal 6:8).

8.6.2.en: "It hath no stalk: the bud shall yield no meal" [7]... They spent all their effort in sowing and planting, but they did not gather a crop that would provide flour for eating. Their crop was like the ears that Pharaoh saw in the dream, exceedingly thin, blasted by the east wind.

8.6.3.en: "If so be it yield, the strangers shall swallow it up" [7]. Even if it yielded a crop, they cannot make use of it, for strangers plunder all their harvest. They surrendered themselves to strange gods, which do not give but swallow up, and do not bless but defile.

8.7.0.en: Would that they had lost only their labor in sowing and reaping, so that even what they managed to gather the strangers swallowed up; but they also lost their dignity, and became despised and rejected by the very nations whom they imitated, whose gods they worshipped, and whose evil spirit they followed. "Now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure. For they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself" [8-9]. Since they keep pace with the nations in their evil, the nations hold them in contempt, and while they take refuge in Assyria, Assyria looks upon them as a wild ass alone by himself. They became like a wild ass, having lost their gentleness, love and tenderness by separating themselves from their God, the giver of the holy and virtuous life. They bore a spirit of isolation instead of the spirit of love that salts the earth so that it does not corrupt; they became corrupt, good for nothing but to be trodden under foot of men (Mt 5:13).

8.7.1.en: Sin strips the soul of its spiritual splendor even in the eyes of the wicked, and creates in it a spirit of inner isolation and selfishness instead of true, self-giving love.

8.8.0.en: "Ephraim hath hired lovers" [9], that is, Ephraim offered much to the nations to win their friendship, but his evil made him lose his awe-inspiring dignity and spiritual beauty even in the eyes of these hirelings. Therefore, at the proper time they did not support Ephraim or Israel but swallowed them up [8], and the need arose not for human flattery but for the strong hand of God, which alone is able to deliver them from the harsh bondage: "Now will I gather them, and they shall be released a little from the burden of the king of princes" [10].

8.9.s.en: 4. Their summons to the first bondage

8.9.0.en: 11 "Because Ephraim hath made many altars to sin, altars shall be unto him to sin. 12 I have written to him the great things of my law, but they were counted as a strange thing. 13 They sacrifice flesh for the sacrifices of mine offerings, and eat it; but the LORD accepteth them not; now will he remember their iniquity, and visit their sins: they shall return to Egypt. 14 For Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and buildeth temples; and Judah hath multiplied fenced cities: but I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall devour the palaces thereof."

8.10.0.en: Since they wanted to please the nations and win their friendship and affection, they made for themselves pagan altars on which they practiced abominations side by side with their worship of God. Therefore God rejected their worship and their offerings and counted their sacrifices as mere meat and eating... "They sacrifice flesh for the sacrifices of mine offerings, and eat it; but the LORD accepteth them not" [13]. They left God their Savior and leaned on the nations; therefore God leaves them, and they revert to their first bondage, from which He had delivered them... "For Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and buildeth temples; and Judah hath multiplied fenced cities: but I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall devour the palaces thereof" [14].

9.0.s.en: 1. The turning of their worship into bread of sorrow

9.0.0.en: 1 Rejoice not, O Israel, for joy, as other people: for thou hast gone a whoring from thy God, thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor. 2 The floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the new wine shall fail in her. 3 They shall not dwell in the LORD'S land; but Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean things in Assyria. 4 They shall not offer wine offerings to the LORD, neither shall they be pleasing unto him: their sacrifices shall be unto them as the bread of mourners; all that eat thereof shall be polluted: for their bread for their soul shall not come into the house of the LORD. 5 What will ye do in the solemn day, and in the day of the feast of the LORD? 6 For, lo, they are gone because of destruction: Egypt shall gather them up, Memphis shall bury them: the pleasant places for their silver, nettles shall possess them: thorns shall be in their tabernacles.

9.0.1.en: "Rejoice not, O Israel, for joy, as other people: for thou hast gone a whoring from thy God, thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor. The floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the new wine shall fail in her" [1-2].

9.0.2.en: Israel thought that the surrounding peoples, with their idolatrous worship marked by many feasts, abominations and revelry, had more luck and joy than he did, so he longed to imitate these peoples and walk after their pattern. But even if the peoples rejoice and are filled with joy amid abominations... this is only an outward show accompanied by inward grief and gloom. Israel, in imitating these peoples, is counted an adulterer against his God, and so falls under bitter discipline. God chose him as a people for Himself, bound to His holy law, and if he deviated he played the part of an adulteress who deserves stoning. So to this day, whenever a believer falls into sin, discipline comes upon him more swiftly and more severely than it comes upon the wicked, because he is chosen by God and is His son who must submit to His discipline. The psalmist says: "Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity... Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart" (Ps 37:1, 4).

9.0.3.en: Man thinks that going after his lusts will satisfy him, saying: "I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oil and my drink" (Hos 2:5). This is the reward that man desires to receive from other gods, preferring it to the Lord's blessing declared in "every cornfloor." He seeks the transient temporal reward rather than the Lord's lasting blessing in the granaries of wheat that satisfy his soul, and so he loses both, for the floor and the winepress do not feed him, and the new wine, in which he thought was his joy and delight, fails him.

9.0.4.en: Historically, this was fulfilled in the life of this people, who ran after the abominations of the nations around them, and so fell into the captivity of Assyria and were deprived of their freedom, their possessions and the good things of their land, and were also deprived of the worship of the living God; they lost both earthly pleasures and spiritual blessings.

9.0.5.en: Their deprivation of joy is the natural fruit of their adultery against their God. God does not accept their worship, nor their drink offering of wine (a sign of joy), nor is He pleased with their sacrifices, so their offerings become rejected and unclean because they come from a spiritual adulterer. These offerings turn into "bread of sorrow" that returns to them to eat in bitterness, instead of being received as a pleasing aroma.

9.1.0.en: The punishment does not stop at depriving them of joy and satisfaction, but reaches final expulsion from the Lord's land, which He had formerly given them as a promised land flowing with milk and honey, saying: "They shall not dwell in the LORD'S land," for they are carried into captivity, and there they are deprived of everything: "They shall not offer wine offerings to the LORD, neither shall they be pleasing unto him: their sacrifices shall be unto them as the bread of mourners; all that eat thereof shall be polluted: for their bread for their soul shall not come into the house of the LORD" [4]. In the land of captivity they live as in an unclean land, having nothing pure that they could offer to the holy Lord! They had formerly been in the holy land of the Lord, and when their hearts withdrew outside the house of the Lord and they brought abominations into the sanctuaries, they were driven out of the sanctuaries and deprived of practicing a pure worship acceptable to the Lord.

9.1.1.en: I say that this is a bitter picture of the unfaithful soul, which the Lord brings in, not to a promised land, but establishing His Kingdom within it, giving it His holy blood as a sign of its salvation and granting it His Spirit dwelling in it. Yet in unfaithfulness it breaks the new covenant and attaches itself to abominations, despising God's surpassing gifts, as the Apostle Paul says: "He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?" (Heb 10:28-29)... Such a person loses the gifts that God gave him, and the blessings of the New Covenant become a mystery of judgment and a witness against him. Such a soul, if it offers any worship whatsoever, God does not accept it so long as it persists in its betrayal of the covenant and the uncleanness of its heart, but returns it to the soul as bread of sorrow. Therefore St. John Chrysostom says: [It is not fitting to offer a sacrifice from something unclean, for it is counted as the firstfruits of the other works. Let us offer our hands and feet and mouth and all our members (pure) as the firstfruits of God, so that they may be counted a cause of God's pleasure.]

9.1.2.en: St. Cyprian speaks of the sacrifices rejected by God and returned to those who offer them as bread of sorrow for them; they are the teachings of the heretics, their worship and their baptism, and he says: [Here He teaches us clearly about those who have been joined to sin altogether, defiled by the sacrifice of an unclean, wicked priest], and he also says: [Here He teaches us about those who unite with condemned leaders, since they are defiled with them by their crimes.]

9.2.0.en: Thus the priests in Israel offered sacrifices to God while their hearts were bound to Baal, so He returned their sacrifices to them as bread of sorrow, and expelled them entirely from the house of the Lord by their captivity to Assyria. And lest the hearers say that what the prophet says is a mere theoretical threat that will not be fulfilled in practice, he continues his speech: "What will ye do in the solemn day, and in the day of the feast of the LORD? For, lo, they are gone because of destruction: Egypt shall gather them up, Memphis shall bury them: the pleasant places for their silver, nettles shall possess them: thorns shall be in their tabernacles" [5-6].

9.2.1.en: They say: In every season and on the feasts of the Lord we gather in the house of the Lord, rejoicing and exulting with psalms and praises, so how does the prophet say that our sacrifices return to us as bread of sorrow? We spend our days in revelry and joy, not in grief and bitterness. The prophet answers that he sees destruction coming swiftly from Assyria, so they take refuge with Pharaoh of Egypt and flee to the land from which the Lord had formerly released them, to die there in Memphis, its capital (Moph). Thus they lose God's promises to them, which are His word (the silver), and in its place they inherit nettles (rust), and their houses in the Promised Land are laid waste and turned into a wilderness that produces brambles and thorns.

9.2.2.en: If God offered us promises of silver that does not rust, and established for us spiritual houses in which we dwell joyfully and securely, yet deviation of the heart from Him turns us from silver to rust and from houses to a wilderness with its brambles and thorns! Thus man loses God's inner peace and the gladness and joy of his heart, and even loses his life, to be buried like a stranger in Moph, and his life turns to rust and his inner house to a wilderness!

9.2.3.en: Symbolically, we may say that silver signifies the soul and the house signifies the body in which the soul dwells, as though, when man runs after temporal joy and revelry like the pagan peoples, with the amusements of the world and the love of luxury, he loses his silver soul, which then rusts, and loses the sanctity of his body, which comes again under the curse, growing thorns and brambles.

9.3.s.en: 2. The arrival of the time of punishment

9.3.0.en: 7 The days of visitation are come, the days of recompence are come; Israel shall know it: the prophet is a fool, the spiritual man is mad, for the multitude of thine iniquity, and the great hatred. 8 The watchman of Ephraim was with my God: but the prophet is a snare of a fowler in all his ways, and hatred in the house of his God. 9 They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah: therefore he will remember their iniquity, he will visit their sins.

9.3.1.en: Israel imagined that it was living in the pleasures of the nations and its own lusts, with joy and revelry, and did not realize that the time of punishment had come: "The days of visitation are come, the days of recompence are come" [7]. The time had come in which Israel is repaid for its evil and the prophets are rewarded for their true witness and for their endurance of reproaches and sufferings from them: "Israel shall know it: the prophet is a fool, the spiritual man is mad, for the multitude of thine iniquity, and the great hatred" [7]. Let Israel know that the one they thought a fool is the bearer of the spirit of wisdom, and the one they counted mad is the man of the Spirit, and that the multitude of its iniquity and the multitude of its hatred corrupted its insight so that it did not recognize the prophet, the man of the Spirit. On the other hand, Israel will discover that the false prophet who flatters them with soft words, saying, "Peace, peace; when there is no peace" (Jer 6:14), is truly the fool, and the one who claimed to be a man of the Spirit is truly mad, since he left Israel in its iniquity, soothing its feelings at the expense of the truth. Thus the true prophet, who may wound with the words of truth for the sake of edification, is distinguished from the deceitful prophet, who is "a snare of a fowler in all his ways" [8]. He catches souls with honeyed words, and is full of hatred against the house of his God [8].

9.4.0.en: The time of recompense has come for them to discover that "they have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah" [9]. A Levite lodged as a stranger at Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin (Judg 19:14), and the men of the city committed evil with his concubine all the night until the morning, and let her go at the dawning of the day, when she came to the door of the house and gave up her spirit. The man took her and cut her into twelve pieces and sent her throughout all the borders of Israel, that they might see the vileness and abomination that had been in that place (Judg 20:6). If the incident of Gibeah exposed the evil, so the time of recompense comes to expose the hidden things of the people!

9.5.0.en: 10 I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time: but they went to Baalpeor, and separated themselves unto that shame; and their abominations were according as they loved. 11 As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception. 12 Though they bring up their children, yet will I bereave them, that there shall not be a man left: yea, woe also to them when I depart from them! 13 Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place: but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer. 14 Give them, O LORD: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.

9.5.1.en: Israel lost inner spiritual joy: first, because of their seeking the revelry of the peoples and the amusements of the nations, committing adultery against their God, so their worship turned into bread of sorrow [1, 6]; and second, because the time of recompense had come for them to discover the error of their standards, so that the one they thought mad and a fool proved to be the true prophet, and the one they counted a prophet who soothed their feelings proved to be the mad fool [7, 9]; and the third reason for their loss of joy is the change in the nature of Israel: instead of being grapes in the wilderness and the firstripe of the fig tree, he gave himself up to shame, and became in his nature an abomination through his passion, for He says: "I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time: but they went to Baalpeor, and separated themselves unto that shame; and their abominations were according as they loved" [10]. We have already commented on this passage in the introduction to the book.

9.5.2.en: Instead of Israel being delicious grapes in the eyes of God in the midst of a barren wilderness, and a firstripe fig, he became by his passion a devoted offering and food for Baal-peor, which means "Baal of debauchery" or "lord of debauchery." He surrendered himself by his passion to Satan, the lord of debauchery, and so turned from the state of fruitfulness that gladdened God and himself to a state of barrenness. His nature turned from a joyful nature to a nature filled with gloom and bitterness of soul.

9.6.0.en: Their attachment to Baal-peor destroyed their nature and also stripped them of their dignity and brought them into disgrace and shame, so that there is no state of birth among them, for their women do not conceive but are barren; and if they conceive and bear, God Himself bereaves them, pronouncing death upon their children, for He says: "Their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception. Though they bring up their children, yet will I bereave them, that there shall not be a man left" [11-12]. Ephraim, in his evil, has become like a bird that flies continually, with no nest in which to settle to lay eggs and have young! It is a painful picture of the man whom sin draws away from his true nest, which is "the altar of the LORD of hosts," to wander in the air without rest, spending the days of his exile without repose or security, and he has no young, that is, no spiritual fruit that immortalizes his name in eternity. This barrenness is the natural fruit of fleeing from the divine nest and turning away from God, the giver of fruit... for when they turn away from Him, He turns away from them, and they fall under the eternal woe: "yea, woe also to them when I depart from them!" [12].

9.7.0.en: Israel fell into a state of barrenness through its worship of Baal and Ashtaroth, since it believed them to be the gods of fruitfulness and fertility; therefore the prophet says: "Give them, O LORD: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts" [14].

9.8.s.en: 4. Their expulsion from before the Lord

9.8.0.en: 15 All their wickedness is in Gilgal: for there I hated them: for the wickedness of their doings I will drive them out of mine house, I will love them no more: all their princes are revolters. 16 Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up, they shall bear no fruit: yea, though they bring forth, yet will I slay even the beloved fruit of their womb. 17 My God will cast them away, because they did not hearken unto him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations.

9.9.0.en: Finally, since Israel ran after Baal and Ashtaroth to give it fertility and fruit, it received the miscarrying womb and the dry breasts... What is more bitter is that God drives it out from before His face and deprives it of His holy house. "For the wickedness of their doings I will drive them out of mine house, I will love them no more" [16], so that it can no longer bear fruit, and if it does bear fruit, the Lord slays it from its beginning in the womb, that is, while it is still an embryo. They despised God and did not hearken to Him, and so He treats them lightly and leaves them wandering among the nations without honor [17]. This is the picture of the soul of every believer who forgets the law of his God and seeks the amusements and delights of the world, and so loses everything and becomes like a wanderer in the world without purpose.
